description: What the main window is permitted to do.
comment: SECURITY: capabilities are granted as they become necessary, never in
advance. `core:default` is the minimum a window needs to exist.
The dialog permissions let the window ask the user to pick a file. Note
what is *not* here: no fs: permission of any kind. Reading and writing go
through this crate's own commands, so the webview can only touch a path a
person chose in a native picker -- never a directory, never a glob, and
never a path the page composed for itself.
`opener:allow-open-url` lets a link inside a document be handed to the
operating system. SECURITY 2 requires exactly that and forbids the
alternative: a link opened in the webview is a link running in the
application's own origin. The URL is sanitized before it gets here and
the user confirms each one -- the permission grants the mechanism, not
the decision.
`core:window:allow-set-title` puts the file name and the unsaved marker
in the native title bar. `core:default` does not include it, and the
call failed silently in the browser build because the desktop branch
never runs there -- it took running the real application to see.
`core:window:allow-destroy` is what actually closes the window. Listening
for a close request makes the webview responsible for the close as well
as for vetoing it, so without this the unsaved-changes guard turned into
a window that could not be shut: clicking the close button rejected and
did nothing. `core:default` grants neither, and the browser build never
reaches this path.
